title: US Lifts Restrictions on Mexican Airlines
author: Arturo Sánchez Jiménez
content:
_This article by[Arturo Sánchez
Jiménez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez%20Jim%C3%A9nez)
originally appeared in the [October 16, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/16/economia/eu-levanta-
restricciones-a-aerolineas-mexicanas), Mexico's premier left wing daily
newspaper._

The United States **Department of Transportation (DOT)** lifted this Friday,
with immediate effect, the restrictions that prevented Mexican airlines from
opening new flights to that country from the **Felipe Ángeles International
Airport (AIFA)** and the Benito Juárez International Airport of Mexico City
(AICM).

In a joint statement, the Secretariats of Foreign Affairs (SRE) and of
Infrastructure, Communications and Transportation (SICT) reported that the
decision was adopted "as a result of the coordinated work between the
Government of Mexico and that of the United States, as well as of the progress
achieved in fulfilling bilateral commitments on aviation."

The measure revokes **Order 213-2** , through which the DOT "had restricted
existing, proposed and future operations of Mexican carriers." According to
the agencies, the determination "represents a significant advance for air
connectivity between both countries" and "once again opens the possibility of
developing routes and frequencies from the AICM and the AIFA to the US
market."

The federal government attributed the result to a process of dialogue and
technical cooperation strengthened since the Memorandum of Consultations
signed in May 2026. "Since then, Mexico has advanced on the agreed
commitments," it stated.

The SRE and the SICT maintained that the decision reflects the will of both
governments to advance toward "a new stage of the bilateral relationship on
aviation, based on dialogue, **respect for sovereignty** , institutional
cooperation, the application of the best international practices and the
permanent strengthening of the safety and efficiency of air transport."

The restriction was announced on October 28, 2025, by the then head of the
DOT, Sean Duffy, and affected **Aeroméxico, Volaris and Viva Aerobus**.
Washington accused Mexico of failing to comply with the bilateral air
transport agreement and of favoring local companies in the allocation of
slots, and pointed to the decree that moved cargo flights from the AICM to the
AIFA as the origin of the conflict. At the time, President Claudia Sheinbaum
maintained that this relocation had been "a technical decision, not a
political one."

In the statement, Mexico committed to continue working with US authorities to
"generate greater opportunities for passengers, workers and airlines, as well
as to consolidate a safe, competitive, modern and reliable aviation system."
